questions.solution: The real solutions of $4^{\text {th }}$ root of unity is $\pm$1 $\therefore \alpha=1, \beta=-1$ and other roots are $\pm i\begin{aligned} & \gamma=i \& \delta=-i \\ & \therefore|z-1|+|z+1|=4 \\ & \Rightarrow|x+i y-1|+|x-i y+1|=4 \\ & \Rightarrow|(x-1)+i y|+|(x+1)-i y|=4 \\ & \Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{(x-1)^2+y^2}=4-\sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2} \\ & \Rightarrow(x-1)^2+y^2=16+(x+1)^2+y^2-8 \sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2} \\ & \Rightarrow-4 x=16-8 \sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2} \\ & \Rightarrow 2 \sqrt{(x+1)^2+y^2}=4+x \end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 4(x+1)^2+4 y^2=(4+x)^2 \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{4}+\frac{y^2}{3}=1 \end{aligned}$ which is an ellipse whose eccentricity is $\Rightarrow e_1=\sqrt{1-\frac{3}{4}}=\frac{1}{2}$ Now, $|z-\gamma|+|z+\delta|=6\Rightarrow|z-i|+|z+i|=6\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow|x+i(y-1)|+|x+i(y+1)|=6 \\ & \Rightarrow \sqrt{x^2+(y-1)^2}+\sqrt{x^2(y+1)^2}=6 \end{aligned}\Rightarrow x^2+(y-1)^2=36+x^2+(y+1)^2-12 \sqrt{x^2+(y+1)^2}\Rightarrow 12 \sqrt{x^2+(y+1)^2}=36+4 y\Rightarrow 9\left(x^2+(y+1)^2\right)=(9+y)^2\Rightarrow \frac{x^2}{8}+\frac{y^2}{9}=1$ which is an ellipse whose essentricity is: $e_2=\sqrt{1-\frac{8}{9}}=\frac{1}{3}$ Now, $e_1+e_2=\frac{1}{2}+\frac{1}{3}=\frac{5}{6}$

options: A straight line that does not contain the point $(-1+i)$
A circle that does not contain the point $(-1+i)$

questions.solution: Given condition is \left|\frac{z-1+i}{z+1-i}\right|=\left|\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1+i}{z+1-i}\right)\right|, z \neq-1+i$ Let $z=x+i y$, then $\begin{aligned} & \frac{z-1+i}{z+1-i}=\frac{(x-1)+i(y+1)}{(x+1)+i(y-1)} \times \frac{(x+1)-i(y-1)}{(x+1)-i(y-1)} \\ & =\frac{\left[\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right]+i[(x+1)(y+1)-(x-1)}{(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2}\end{aligned}$ So, \left|\frac{z-1+i}{z+1-i}\right|=\sqrt{\frac{\left[\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right]^2+(2(x+y))^2}{\left((x+1)^2+(y-1)^2\right)^2}}$ and \left|\operatorname{Re}\left(\frac{z-1+i}{z+1-i}\right)\right|=\frac{\left|\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right|}{(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2}$ Now, according to given condition $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\sqrt{\left(\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right)^2+(2(x+y))^2}}{(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2} \\ & =\frac{\left|\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right|}{(x+1)^2+(y-1)^2} \\ & \Rightarrow \quad\left(\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right)^2+4(x+y)^2 \\ & =\left(\left(x^2-1\right)+\left(y^2-1\right)\right)^2\end{aligned}\Rightarrow x+y=0$ is a straight line, but as $z \neq-1+i$ so locus of $z$ is a straight line that does not contain the point $(-1+i)$. Hence, option (a) is correct.$

questions.q: If $e^{i\theta} = cis\theta$~then~$\mathop{∑}_{n = 0}^{∞}\dfrac{cos\left(n\theta\right)}{2n} =$
questions.solution:
Let

$C = \mathop{∑}_{n = 0}^{∞}\dfrac{cosn\theta}{2n}$

$⇒ C = 1 + \dfrac{cos\left(\theta\right)}{2} + \dfrac{cos\left(2\theta\right)}{22} + \dfrac{cos\left(3\theta\right)}{23} + . . . .$

$iS = \dfrac{isin\left(\theta\right)}{2} + \dfrac{isin\left(2\theta\right)}{22} + \dfrac{isin\left(3\theta\right)}{23} + . . . .$

Then,

$C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}\left(cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{22}\left(cos2\theta + isin2\theta\right) + \dfrac{1}{23}\left(cos3\theta + isin3\theta\right) + . . . .$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}e^{i\theta} + \dfrac{1}{22}e^{2i\theta} + \dfrac{1}{23}e^{3i\theta} + . . . . . .$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2}e^{i\theta}}{1 - \dfrac{1}{2}e^{i\theta}}$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{ei\theta}{2 - e^{i\theta}}$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \dfrac{cos\theta + isin\theta}{2 - cos\theta - isin\theta}$

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\left(\dfrac{cos\theta + isin\theta}{2 - cos\theta - isin\theta}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{2 - cos\theta + isin\theta}{2 - cos\theta + isin\theta}\right)\right]

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\dfrac{cos\theta\left(2 - cos\theta + isin\theta\right) + isin\theta \left($2 - $cos\theta ++isin\theta\rright)}{\left($2 - $cos\theta\right)$2 + $\sin^{2}\theta}\right]

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + \left[\dfrac{2cos\theta - \cos^{2}\theta - \sin^{2}\theta + 2isin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right]

$⇒ C + iS = 1 + $\$left[\dfrac{2cos\theta - 1 + 2isin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right]

$⇒ C + iS = \left[\dfrac{4 - 2cos\theta + 2isin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right]

$⇒ C + iS = $\$left(\dfrac{4 - 2cos\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right) +$i \left(\dfrac{2sin\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}\right)$

On comparing real and imaginary part, we get

$C = \dfrac{4 - 2cos\theta}{5 - 4cos\theta}$

questions.solution:
According to given information $|z-2 i|=2$ is a circle having centre is $(0,2)$ and radius is 2 .
If the area of $\triangle A B C$ is maximum the triangle must be equilateral triangle and point $M$ is the mid point of $B C$, where $M$ is the foot of perpendicular of point $A \left(z_1=2+2 i\right)$ on $B C$. $\therefore$ Sum of the imaginary parts of $z_2$ and $z_3$ is twice of the imaginary part of $M=2 \times 2=4.$
